topics.topic: Startup handling and ordering when a valid SQLite store is not in WAL mode
questions: When an existing, restored or newly created same-version store is not already in write-ahead-log mode, must startup change it to WAL, refuse to serve, or accept it on the assumption that deployment prepared it? At what point in A17's ordered startup procedure is that done or checked?
What must Registry do when the configured store is valid and of the running release's version but is not in write-ahead-log mode?
What must startup do when an otherwise valid store is not in WAL mode: refuse it, change it to WAL before serving, or serve it despite A18?

quotes:
The store runs in SQLite's write-ahead-log mode, in which a reader and the writer never
   wait for each other, so no write waits for, or is refused or fails for,
   a copy, nor a copy for a write.

otherwise
   the store must open for reading and writing, pass the full integrity check
   — the store is a SQLite database, as v1's (L19), and the check passes when
   `PRAGMA integrity_check` answers `ok` and `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` finds
   nothing, the same as a backup's check (A18 rule 4) — and carry
   the store
   version of the running release, and a store of another version, or one
   that does not open, fails the start — bringing a store to a new version is
   a step of the release, not of the start.
judgement.divergence: One implementation changes the valid store to WAL mode during the store-opening step and serves; another refuses startup because the store is not already in WAL mode, and the owner observes a successful start with a modified store versus a failed start.
judgement.why: A18 requires WAL operation, but the exhaustive A17 startup checks neither prescribe conversion nor make non-WAL mode a refusal condition.

witness.initial: The owner has placed a writable, correct-version SQLite store that passes both integrity checks but uses rollback-journal mode at the configured store location.
events: The owner starts Registry with an otherwise valid configuration.
Registry reaches A17's store-opening step and inspects the existing store.
outcomes: Registry changes the journal mode to WAL and serves.
Registry refuses startup because the store was not already in WAL mode.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether Registry starts and whether the store is changed.
basis:
A store the owner puts in
   place of a lost one starts as any store (A17 rule 5) — by the release that
   made its backup, or by a later one after that release's own store
   migration — and begins its own history from the backup: numbering
   continues from its last number (A15), and a store without the migration
   closure accepts the import (A16).

otherwise
   the store must open for reading and writing, pass the full integrity check
   — the store is a SQLite database, as v1's (L19), and the check passes when
   `PRAGMA integrity_check` answers `ok` and `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` finds
   nothing, the same as a backup's check (A18 rule 4) — and carry
   the store
   version of the running release, and a store of another version, or one
   that does not open, fails the start — bringing a store to a new version is
   a step of the release, not of the start.

topics.topic: Event and ordering that determine the backup snapshot's recorded instant
questions: If the read transaction begins before its first read, which event determines the backup's recorded instant?
Must Registry sample the recorded instant before or after the audit-counter read fixes the SQLite snapshot, and which side of a concurrent commit does that instant represent?

quotes:
A backup is a consistent copy of the store taken while Registry runs:
   one snapshot of the store, as one read transaction sees it, while other
   transactions go on; it never holds part of a transaction, and its
   recorded instant and last sequence number are those of that snapshot,
   the instant being when its read transaction began.

The copy's read transaction fixes its
   snapshot by its first read, which is of the audit counter's last
   sequence number, and the instant is read from the clock at that read; a
   change committed after it is not in this backup, which holds the store as
   its snapshot saw it, and a later backup holds whatever the store holds
   when its own snapshot is fixed.
judgement.why: One passage assigns the recorded instant to the beginning of the read transaction, while the other assigns it to the later first read that fixes the snapshot.

witness.initial: Registry is running with service tokens and a daily backup run is due.
events: Registry begins the backup's read transaction at 03:00:00 UTC.
The worker is delayed before its first database read.
At 03:01:00 UTC it first reads the audit counter and fixes the snapshot.
outcomes: The backup records 03:00:00 UTC because its instant is when the read transaction began.
The backup records 03:01:00 UTC because its instant is read from the clock at the first read.
witness.observer: The owner sees the different instant as the newest kept backup's instant.
basis:
Every day at
   03:00 UTC, while Registry runs with its service tokens, it
   makes one backup run; a 03:00 that finds Registry stopped, or in an
   owner-only start (rule 9), makes no run, and none is made later in its
   place.

The
   owner interface shows the instant of the newest kept backup whose record
   can be read, or that there is none, from one listing of the backup
   location; read while a run renames or deletes, it shows the state before
   or after that change, never a temporary file.
